lesson: An unreadable config.yaml (missing, permission error) returns [] and is treated as 'no presets configured'. The build then proceeds with only base and exits 0, so 'could not read config' reads as 'nothing configured'. Distinguish the missing/unreadable case: warn on stderr and exit non-zero (or at least exit 1).

The parser only understands the inline `[..]` and block-list forms. Any other shape (e.g. `presets: python` scalar, `presets: []` mixed with comments, CRLF line endings, `presets:  # comment` followed by a list, or a `presets:` key nested under another section) silently yields [] and exit 0 instead of flagging a malformed value. Fail closed: if a `presets:` key is present but no form matched, warn and exit 1.

`Extends:` is matched only when the file's first non-blank line is exactly that; the README and header comment say 'start the file with Extends', but a `Extends: x` with trailing text, in different case, or after a `# Preset:` title line is silently ignored and the local file replaces the built-in with no warning. Also `Extends: <other>` where <other> is neither local nor built-in yields (parent, None), reported unknown, but a local preset extending a name that itself extends is silently single-level. Additionally the extends() open() has no error handling (non-UTF-8 file raises a traceback, exit 1 with no 'unknown preset' message).

Tests cover only the inline `[..]` config form. The block-list parser branch, `Extends: other-name` (non-self), local-extends-local, dedupe, missing config, and the Extends-not-first-line case have no tests, so the variants of this resolver are unproven. Also AC-5 only checks the exit code with the `../x` name; it does not verify that no file outside presets/ is read.

AC-6 asserts $TMP/n/.specclaw/presets/README.md exists but the diff never creates $TMP/n in the added lines; it depends on an earlier fixture elsewhere in the file. If that fixture does not run specclaw-init, the check is vacuous or fails for the wrong reason, and it does not verify init content matches the template.

The Extends fix is an instance fix. It added case-insensitivity and heading-skipping, but the named 'trailing text' variant still matches nothing. The regex needs the whole line to be `extends: <one-token>`, so any other line returns None. A local preset then silently replaces the built-in, with no warning and exit 0. A malformed Extends declaration (the line starts with `extends` but does not parse) should be warned and exit 1 instead of being treated as 'no Extends'. Also decide and document what happens when prose or an HTML comment precedes the Extends line.

The block-list branch still fails open for malformed shapes. The loop breaks on the first line that does not start with `- `, so it cannot tell a new top-level key from garbage inside the list. Garbage includes an indented scalar, a bare `-`, `-python` and `- ` with a tab. Everything after that line is silently dropped, and the key then yields a short or empty list with exit 0. Break only on a column-0 non-dash line (a new key). Warn on any other unparsable line under `presets:`.

The variant table still lacks cases the previous round named. There is no dedupe row (`[python, python]` or `[base]`) and no row for Extends placed after non-heading text or carrying trailing text. There is no row for a malformed block list (indented scalar, bare `-`), which would have exposed the B6 gap. The symlink case covers only a direct preset file, not an Extends parent that is a symlink. AC-5 (`../x`) still asserts only the exit code, not that nothing outside presets/ is read.

The AC-6 'fix' is only a comment. It claims the $TMP/n tree comes from an AC-10 case 'above', and that cannot be checked from the diff. The test still depends on a fixture elsewhere in the file. It still asserts only that the README exists, not that its content matches the init template. Drive specclaw-init into a fresh dir within this test and compare the file to the template (`cmp`).

The Extends check is now too broad. It scans every non-heading line in the file, with no fence or position awareness. Any line that starts with the word `extends` is treated as a malformed or misplaced Extends declaration, including ordinary prose. That prose line triggers the warning and an exit-1 failure for a valid preset that never declared Extends. Only a line that looks like a declaration (`extends` followed by optional spaces and a colon) should be an error. A prose line that merely begins with the word should be ignored, and the match should skip fenced code blocks. Add a regression row for this.

The new symlinked-Extends-parent check only asserts `! specclaw-presets | grep -q outside.md`, with no exit-code assertion. The sibling direct-symlink check has both. Output lines are label-style (`v:a`, `specclaw:base`), so the symlink named b.md would print as `v:b` or a b.md path and never contain `outside.md`. The grep is then vacuously true even if the symlink guard were removed for Extends parents. Assert exit 1 and the exact stdout (`specclaw:base v:a `). Better still, assert that the parent's content ('secret') is absent from the build output.

A file that does not open with `---` now returns None silently. This includes the old `Extends: <name>` first-line form, any case or spelling variant, and the common mistake of using `extends:` without frontmatter. The local file then silently replaces the built-in, which is the wrong-intent fallback the earlier rounds treated as an error. The prose-collision fix should have kept a narrow check: warn and exit 1 only when a non-heading line outside any fence matches `^extends\s*:`, as the previous round proposed. Prose such as 'Extends the base rules.' would still pass.

The fix only handles part of the fenced-code case. `stray()` treats only a line starting with three backticks as a fence. Three variants are wrong: (1) a `~~~` fence is not recognised, so a documented `extends: node` inside it is reported as an error, which is a false positive that blocks the whole build. (2) Every line is `.strip()`ped before the check, so an indented code block or an indented list continuation line `    extends: node` is also flagged. (3) An unclosed ``` fence hides every later line, so a real stray `extends:` after it is silently ignored. That is the fail-open case this fix was meant to close. Track the fence character and length, and close only on a matching fence. Check the indentation-sensitive form on the raw line instead of the stripped one. Warn when a fence is still open at end of file.

The variant table for the stray-`extends:` check covers only the backtick fence. It has no rows for a `~~~` fence, an indented `extends:` line, an unclosed fence followed by `extends:`, `Extends : node` with a space before the colon, or a heading containing the word. Without these rows the instance fix above passes while the variants misbehave. Add them to the table.

The variants the previous round named are still missing from the table. Only one row asserts that the warning is emitted (`# Ours\nExtends: node`). The other stray rows (not-on-line-1, after-fm, the fenced row) assert only `exit 0` plus the label list, and those are identical whether `stray()` warns or not. Add warning-assertion rows for: a `~~~` fence, an unclosed fence followed by `extends:`, `Extends : node` with a space before the colon, and a heading containing the word. Add negative rows asserting no warning for an indented `    extends: node` and for valid frontmatter. Also make the new check create its own `$TMP/v` fixture instead of reusing the directory left by the previous `cfgcase`. The explicit `printf` writes are fine, but the dir and `presets/` must exist from earlier cases.

Extends is followed only one level, and the parent's own frontmatter is never read or checked. When a local preset extends another local preset that has its own frontmatter, that parent's `extends:` is silently dropped and the run exits 0. A malformed parent frontmatter (other key, unclosed) is not reported either. The README shows both `extends: dotnet` inside dotnet.md and adding a new `acme-dotnet`, so chaining them is the obvious use, and the README never says 'one level'. Fix: run `extends()` on a local parent too. Either follow it, with a cycle guard, or warn fatally that a nested extends is ignored. Add rows for a two-level chain, a malformed parent frontmatter and a self or mutual cycle.

`lookup` returns None for 'no such file' and also for 'a file is there but cannot be used': a dangling symlink, a directory named `<name>.md`, or a non-regular file. `resolve` reads None as 'no local preset' and silently substitutes the built-in. Fix: if `os.path.lexists(p)` is true but the path is not a usable regular file, warn fatally and do not fall back. Add rows for a dangling symlink and for a directory.

The BOM handling (`utf-8-sig`) was applied to preset files but not to config.yaml, which is read as plain `utf-8`. A BOM-prefixed first line `\ufeffpresets: [..]` fails `^presets:`. `configured()` then returns [] exactly as if no presets were configured, and exits 0. Fix: open config.yaml with `utf-8-sig`. Add a 'BOM before presets:' row next to the existing CRLF rows.

The nested-extends check treats any parent with frontmatter as nesting. That includes a local parent that only extends its own built-in (`dotnet.md` with `extends: dotnet`), which is the documented way to keep a built-in. A valid two-file setup therefore fails the build, and when only the child is listed the built-in parent is silently dropped from the output. Exempt `extends(local_parent) == parent` and emit the built-in before the local parent, or warn non-fatally when that parent is already resolved earlier in `out`. Add table rows for both orders.

Scalar parsing exists twice and the copies disagree. `strip()` (config values) strips any mix of quote characters, while `extends()` uses a regex with a back-reference that requires matched quotes. The same malformed value is accepted in config.yaml and rejected in frontmatter, so config fails open (B6). Share one value parser that rejects mismatched quotes, and add config rows for `"node'` and `'node`.

Comment stripping only recognises a space before `#` (`split(" #")`), in both `strip()` and the frontmatter line at line 102. YAML also allows a tab before `#`, and a value with a tab-led comment is then rejected as malformed or unknown. Strip comments on `\s#` in the shared parser and add tab-comment rows for flow, block and frontmatter.

The first `tool.call` handler awaits `next(e)`, which runs the tool, and then calls `refresh($)`. Its `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))` calls `next(e)` again without checking `next.called`. If `refresh` throws after the tool has run, the tool call is dispatched a second time. The gate handler below guards this case with `!next.called`; this one does not. Fix by making the catch return the already-obtained result when `next.called`, or by wrapping only the `refresh` call in try/catch. No test drives `register.tsx` at all.

`readJson` returns `null` for the text `null`, but `parseChange` only checks `json === undefined`. `json.phase` then throws a TypeError. Other valid non-object JSON (`42`, `[]`, `"x"`) gets phase `proposal` instead of `?`. `refresh` has no catch at the session.start, turn.complete or command.run call sites, so one bad state.json breaks the status line, band and pane for every change. AC2 only tests unparsable text. Treat any non-object JSON as malformed (`?`) and add table rows for `null`, `42`, `[]` and `"s"`.

`normalise` and `relativeInside` handle only POSIX `/` paths. On Windows, `cwd` like `C:\proj` and `path` like `C:\proj\src\a.ts` never produce an inside-the-project relative path, so `relativeInside` returns undefined and the gate returns ALLOW. The guard is silently disabled while it appears active. A path that cannot be resolved should fail closed (deny or warn), or backslashes should be normalised first.

The double-dispatch fix has no test. The previous round noted that no test drives register.tsx, and none was added. The catch now swallows every refresh error with `.catch(() => undefined)`. Add a test that drives the real `tool.call` handler with a stub `next` and a refresh that rejects, and assert that `next` is called exactly once and the tool result is returned. Also cover a refresh that throws synchronously, because `.catch` does not intercept that and the error would escape after the tool has run.

Paths are compared case-sensitively, so a differently-cased spelling of a project path is treated as outside the project and the gate returns ALLOW. The previous finding asked for unresolvable paths to fail closed. The fix handles backslashes only, and the README now documents the case gap as a known limitation. Windows and default macOS filesystems are case-insensitive, so this is a bypass of the gate. Compare case-insensitively on those platforms. Alternatively, deny or warn when the path cannot be shown to be outside the project.

The state.json carve-out is covered by a single row. A table should add other spellings and shapes: `.specclaw/state.json`, a traversal such as `/repo/.specclaw/x/../changes/y/state.json`, the backslash form `.specclaw\changes\x\state.json`, warn mode, and an allow row for a non-state file under `.specclaw`. The Windows table has no allow rows, such as a `D:\other` path outside the project or `.specclaw\x.md`, and no mixed-case row.

The diff changes plugin code (hooks/core/gate.ts, README, tests) under plugins/specclaw-mod/ but bumps no version. Bump specclaw-mod, and every other plugin, to the same version in each plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, each plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.

The glob `./tests/*.spec.ts` excludes register.test.ts. That file imports 'claude-code/testing' and runs only under `claude plugin test`. When `claude` is not on PATH the script sets RESULT=PARTIAL but still exits 0. A runner that has skipped the only test for the double-dispatch fix therefore reports success. Exit non-zero (or a distinct code) when the claude-based steps did not run, or fail in CI.

The test covers one failure mode only: the `session.cwd` handler throws. The previous round asked for both a rejecting refresh and a synchronously throwing refresh, because `.catch` does not intercept a synchronous throw. Add rows for both shapes. Assert the returned tool result (`{ result: { stdout: 'ok' } }`), not just `deny === undefined`. The two commands in the loop exercise the same path and add no variant. The test also never runs under `bun test`, so there is no evidence it fails without the fix.

The previous round's R1 finding is not fixed in this diff. The commit changes files under plugins/specclaw-mod/ (README.md, tests/*, run-mod-tests.sh) but touches no plugin.json or marketplace.json. No version bump is present. Bump every plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, every plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to one identical new version. Add a check (for example in ci.yml) that fails when these versions disagree, so the rule holds for all files rather than just this one.

The gate's `.catch(($, e, next) => ...)` returns `next(e)` even when `next.called` is true. It only skips the toast. This is the same double-dispatch defect that was fixed in the first `tool.call` handler; the fix did not reach this second copy. If the gate allowed the edit and the downstream chain or the tool then threw, the catch runs the tool a second time. Fix: when `next.called` is true, rethrow (or return the original failure) instead of calling `next(e)` again. Add a register.test.ts table over: gate allows then the tool throws, gate allows then the tool rejects, and refresh throws before `next`. Assert the Edit/Write runs at most once in each row.

Any failure inside the gate is turned into ALLOW: the catch shows a toast and calls `next(e)`. This covers a rejected `$.session.cwd()`, a rejected `$.fs.exists`, an update failure, and a TypeError from a missing `file_path`. A guard that falls back to the permissive outcome on error goes against fail-closed. The README documents this, but documenting it does not make it safe. Fix: in `block` mode, when `next` has not been called, return `{ deny: 'specclaw: the propose gate could not run; ...' }`. Keep allow-plus-toast only for `warn` mode. Add table rows for a cwd that rejects, a refresh that throws, and an event with no `file_path`.

`readText` maps every read failure to `undefined`, which is the same value as 'file absent'. `$.fs.list(root).catch(() => [])` (line 27) maps a failed listing to 'no changes'. `parseChange` then treats an undefined state as `{}`, which gives phase `proposal`, not `?`. A changes folder that could not be read shows as 'No active specclaw changes.' and 'specclaw: 0 active'. Fix: carry a distinct unread/error marker. A state.json that exists but cannot be read should give phase `?`. A failed listing should give an 'unknown' snapshot that the pane and status line show as 'could not read .specclaw/changes'.

The refresh-failure fix was applied only to the post-tool `tool.call` handler. `session.start` (line 29), `turn.complete` (line 40) and `command.run` (line 34) still `await refresh($)` with no catch. A refresh failure there rejects the handler before `next(e)` runs, so the rest of the chain is skipped. Fix: wrap refresh in these handlers the same way, so that `next(e)` always runs. Add a register.test.ts row for each event in which `session.cwd` throws and rejects, and assert that a downstream handler still runs.

`readText` turns a failed `$.fs.read` into `''`. An empty string means both "the file is empty" and "the file could not be read". For `tasks.md` this also stops the lean fallback, because `'' ?? leanTasks(...)` keeps `''`. The pane and band then show `0/0 tasks` as if the count were known. Return a distinct failure marker, or let the read error reach `parseChange` and mark the change as unreadable (for example tasks `?`), so a failed read never looks like a real zero.

`refreshQuietly` drops every refresh error with `.catch(() => undefined)`. The `snapshot` atom and `$.ui.status` keep the last good values, so stale data looks current. The list-failure path sets `isUnreadable`, but a failure in `session.cwd`, `fs.exists` or `update` gives no sign that the view was not refreshed. In the catch, mark the snapshot (or at least the status line) as unknown, for example by setting `isUnreadable` or the status to `specclaw: could not read changes`.

The fix that keeps each hook's chain running after a failed refresh covers `session.start`, `command.run` and `turn.complete`. The test drives only the first two, and only with a synchronously throwing `session.cwd`. Make it a table over all three hooks × both failure shapes (throws and rejects), matching register.test.ts. Assert that `turn.complete` still reaches downstream `next`.

Path matching is done as text. The fix covers backslashes and letter case but not the other aliases a file system resolves to the same file. These variants pass the gate: (1) a Windows path with no drive letter but rooted at the drive (`\proj\src\a.ts`); (2) an extended-length or UNC prefix (`\\?\C:\proj\...`), which normalise turns into `/?/C:/...`, so `relativeInside` returns undefined and the gate returns ALLOW; (3) a Windows trailing-dot or alternate-data-stream spelling (`state.json.` or `state.json::$DATA`), which slips past `STATE_FILE` and then matches `EXEMPT`; (4) a project path in NFD Unicode on APFS when cwd is in NFC. Canonicalise before comparing: strip `\\?\`, resolve drive-rooted paths against the drive of cwd, apply NFC, and trim trailing dots, spaces and `:stream` suffixes. When a path cannot be resolved against cwd, return deny or warn, not ALLOW. Add rows for each variant to the AC6 table.

The fix 'show unreadable state' (refreshQuietly sets the status to `statusText(UNREADABLE)` and stores UNREADABLE in the snapshot atom) has no test of what it shows. The events and register tests only check that the chain goes on and the tool result is kept. For each event × failure shape row, add a check that the snapshot read afterwards has `isUnreadable: true`, or that the status was set to 'specclaw: could not read changes'. Seed a good snapshot first so the test proves stale data is replaced.

The gate's `.catch` checks `next.called` only to decide whether to show the toast, then calls `next(e)` in both branches. When the gate has already allowed the edit and called `next(e)`, a tool that then throws reaches this catch, and `next(e)` dispatches the tool again. The earlier lesson asked for this exact guard, but only half of it was applied. Fix: when `next.called` is true, rethrow `e` and do not call `next` a second time; call `next(e)` only when `!next.called`. The FR8 test in `tests/events.test.ts:38` does not reach this path. It stubs no `fs.stat`, so `placeInCwd` throws on `cannot resolve` before `next` is ever called, and the test stays green with the bug present. Make it a table that covers three rows: the gate allows because there is no `.specclaw`, the gate allows because a change is approved, and the gate warns. Stub `fs.stat` in each row so the cwd resolves.

The case fix only works for path segments that already exist. `placePath` resolves the existing prefix through `realPath`, but it keeps the trailing segments that don't exist yet exactly as typed. `STATE_FILE` and `EXEMPT` are then matched case-sensitively. On a case-insensitive file system (APFS by default, NTFS), `state.json`, `State.json` and `STATE.JSON` are the same file to the reader (`read.ts` asks for `${dir}/state.json`). The gate treats them as different files. So a Write that creates a change's state file under another spelling counts as an exempt `.specclaw/` file and is allowed. The model can then approve its own proposal, which is exactly what the README says the gate prevents. Fix: match the file name with the `i` flag (`/^\.specclaw\/changes\/[^/]+\/state\.json$/i`) and also match `EXEMPT` case-insensitively. Then add a place.test row for each spelling (`state.json` in a new dir, `State.json`, `STATE.JSON` in an existing dir with no state.json) that expects the Write to be held. Also correct the README's "letter case included" claim, which is only true for segments that exist.

The gate still fails open, and `README.md:30` documents this as deliberate. Any throw before `next` runs ends in the `.catch`, which shows a toast and calls `next(e)`, so the edit is allowed even in `block` mode. Causes include a rejected `$.fs.list` or `$.fs.read` inside `refresh`, `placeInCwd` throwing on an unresolvable cwd, or a failed `update`. The gate calls `refresh($)` directly instead of the UNREADABLE path. Yet `gateDecision` would already hold an edit given `UNREADABLE` (`hasSpecclaw: true`, no approved change), so the safe outcome exists and is skipped. Because `refresh` throws before `$.ui.status`, the status line also keeps the last good value (B3). Fix: when `!next.called`, store and show UNREADABLE, then return `{ deny }` in block mode and toast plus `next(e)` in warn mode. Change the README to match. Add a table test over the failure sources (list rejects, read rejects, cwd unresolvable) × block/warn.

The earlier fix made every hook's chain go on after a failed refresh, but the class is 'a failure in the handler before `next(e)` skips the rest of the chain'. In `session.start`, `await $.command.register(...)` is not guarded. A rejection there rejects the handler before `refreshQuietly` and `next(e)`, so later session.start handlers never run and the snapshot is never loaded. Fix: catch the register failure, or run `next(e)` in a `finally`. Add a `command.register` throws/rejects row to the FR6 table in `events.test.ts`.

`readOrUnknown` turns any failed read of a change's files into a parsed change with phase `?` and `approved: false`. Failures it catches include a rejected `$.fs.read` or `$.fs.stat`, a rejected `$.fs.exists`, and a non-string read. The gate then runs on that snapshot and returns a definite verdict. In `block` mode it denies the edit with "no approved change is open". R2 says a gate read failure must show a toast and allow the edit. Here the read failure blocks work instead, and the message wrongly claims that no approval exists. Fix: record that a change was unreadable, for example with an `isUnreadable` flag on the change or the snapshot, keeping the `?` row for the pane. In `gateDecision`, treat an unreadable change as a gate failure: throw into the existing catch so it shows the toast and allows the edit. Do not count it as not approved. Add a variant test that drives the real `tool.call` path with three failures: `fs.read` rejects, `fs.stat` rejects, and `fs.read` returns a non-string, each on an approved change's `state.json`. Each row must assert that the tool ran and the toast was shown.

`realPathOf` uses `.catch(() => undefined)`, so every `$.fs.stat` failure, including EACCES and EIO, is read as "this path does not exist". `placePath` then walks up to an ancestor and builds the target from the unresolved names. A symbolic link whose stat fails is therefore compared by its text, not by where it points. The gate can then decide the file is outside the project and allow the edit with no toast, which R2 forbids. Fix: map only ENOENT/ENOTDIR to `undefined` and rethrow every other error, so it reaches the gate's catch and its toast. Add table rows to `place.test.ts` where `fs.stat` throws a non-ENOENT error on a link into the project, for example `/link/src/a.ts` and `/link/new/a.ts`.

The state.json hold only applies after the target is resolved and found inside the resolved root. `readSnapshot` (read.ts:31-37) reads approvals from the unresolved `${cwd}/.specclaw/changes/*/state.json`, but `placePath` follows symlinks before the check. If `.specclaw` (or `.specclaw/changes`) is a symlink to a folder outside the project, the resolved target falls outside `root`. `relativeInside` then returns undefined and the gate returns ALLOW (line 44) before the STATE_FILE test runs. The model can then write `approved` into the very file the gate reads, so the self-approval guard the README promises is bypassed. Fix: test the STATE_FILE rule against the path as `readSnapshot` addresses it (the cwd-relative spelling) as well as the resolved target. Alternatively, resolve `.specclaw/changes` once and hold any target under that resolved directory. Add table rows for a `.specclaw` symlink, a `.specclaw/changes` symlink, and a direct path.

The fix that holds a change's state.json when .specclaw is linked outside the project only works when `.specclaw/changes` already exists. `changes` comes from `realPathOf`, which returns undefined for a missing directory. `isStateFile` is then false, and the resolved target (outside the root) falls through `relativeInside(root, …) === undefined` to ALLOW. The same gap applies when a single change folder is a link out of `changes/`: the resolved target is no longer under the resolved `changes`, so it is allowed. Fix: resolve the changes location with the same ancestor walk as the target (`placePath($, cwd, '.specclaw/changes')`). Also classify by the unresolved spelling relative to cwd, so `.specclaw/changes/<x>/state.json` is held however its ancestors resolve.

No test drives the linked-`.specclaw` state.json fix through the real path. The only coverage is `gate.spec.ts`, which passes `changes: '/outside/changes'` to `gateDecision` by hand. `place.test.ts` links `/repo/linked` but never links `.specclaw` or `.specclaw/changes`, and it only has a `spec.md` row for the linked tree. Add `REAL` rows where `/repo/.specclaw` (and, separately, `/repo/.specclaw/changes`) resolve outside the project. Write table rows for `state.json`, `State.json` and a new change folder's `state.json`, each expecting the edit to be held, plus a `spec.md` row expecting it to pass.

The gate-failure toast in `.catch` is neither awaited nor guarded. If `$.ui.toast` throws or rejects, the gate error is never surfaced, yet the edit still runs through `next(e)`. A synchronous throw would also skip `next(e)`. The warn path at line 60 already falls back to `$.ui.status` when the toast fails, but this catch path does not (B1 variant). Fix: `await Promise.resolve().then(() => $.ui.toast(msg)).catch(() => $.ui.status(msg))` before `return next(e)`.

With no approved change, the gate allows a Write that turns the gate itself off. `.specclaw/changes/<n>/state.json/foo` is not matched by STATE_FILE or CHANGE_STATE, so EXEMPT lets it through. The Write creates `state.json` as a directory. On the next refresh, `readText` in read.ts calls `$.fs.read` on that directory, which rejects or returns a non-string. `readOrUnknown` then marks the change `isUnreadable`, and gateDecision throws on every later edit. The R2 catch allows each of those edits with a toast. So the gate runs and returns the wrong verdict (allow) for the planting edit, even in `block` mode. The same class: `tasks.md/foo` and `change.md/foo` under any change dir, since any read failure in `readChange` makes the change unreadable. Fix: hold any path under a change dir that passes through a `state.json`, `tasks.md` or `change.md` component, compared case-insensitively. Add a table-driven Write test over the three names.

Commit a43e1db holds writes that would break the gate's own reads, such as turning a change's tasks.md or change.md into a folder. It misses the parent of that layout. When `.specclaw/` exists and `.specclaw/changes` does not, a Write to `.specclaw/changes` itself is EXEMPT and allowed. After that, `readSnapshot` calls `$.fs.list` on a regular file, every `refresh` throws, and every later Edit or Write fails open with a toast. Fix: hold any write whose relative path is `.specclaw/changes` exactly, and also `.specclaw` while the gate is closed, the same way the `tasks.md/` and `change.md/` cases are held. Add rows for these to place.test.ts.

Commit 4378112 stopped a failed command registration from skipping session.start's chain. The fallback `.catch(() => $.ui.toast(...))` is itself unguarded, so a rejecting toast rejects the handler before `refreshQuietly` and `next(e)` run. Every other toast in this file is wrapped as `Promise.resolve().then(() => $.ui.toast(..)).catch(() => $.ui.status(..))`; use that same wrapper here. Add a row to the events.test.ts table where both command.register and ui.toast fail.

The fixes in a43e1db and 88d6d28 hold writes that would leave a change file the mod cannot read, but they only cover changes to the folder layout. They miss writes that make the content unreadable. `readText` throws when `fs.read` returns a non-string (tests/failopen.test.ts treats `{ base64 }` as a real answer). `readOrUnknown` then marks the whole change `isUnreadable`, and `gateDecision` throws. A plain Write or Edit of binary content into `tasks.md` or `change.md` is EXEMPT, so the gate allows it, and from then on every edit fails open (R2). Only `state.json` decides approval. Fix: only a `state.json` read failure should mark a change unreadable for the gate. A `tasks.md` or `change.md` that cannot be read should show as unknown task counts, without making the gate throw.

Writes that replace `.specclaw` or `.specclaw/changes` are caught only by the spelled (lexical) path or by a path relative to the project root. `isStateFile` checks paths *under* the resolved `changes`, never the resolved `changes` folder itself or the resolved `.specclaw`. When `.specclaw` is a link outside the project, a Write to the link target's `changes` path is outside the root, does not match `spelled`, and reaches ALLOW. Fix: hold the target when it equals the resolved `changes` path or the resolved `.specclaw` path (compare without case, as `CHANGE_STATE` does). Add a linked.test row for it.

`readText` gates every read on `$.fs.exists`. That cannot tell "absent" from "could not stat" (EACCES/EIO), and it maps both to `undefined`. A `state.json` the mod cannot stat is then parsed as a missing file: phase `proposal`, mtime 0, 0/0 tasks. The pane and band show this as real data instead of unreadable, and no toast appears. `place.ts` already separates ENOENT/ENOTDIR from other errors; `read.ts` keeps a second, permissive copy of that existence rule (B4). Fix: stat once, treat only ENOENT/ENOTDIR as absent, and rethrow anything else so `readOrUnknown` marks the change unreadable.

An earlier fix had to stop a differently-cased path from escaping the gate. It now relies on `fs.stat({resolve:true}).realPath` to fold case (README: "the letter case of existing folders resolve"). The REAL table has no entry where a differently-cased spelling of an existing folder resolves to the canonical path. The only case row is the non-existent `/repo/.SpecClaw`, which is held for another reason (STATE_FILE /i). If placePath kept the typed case, every row would still pass. Add rows such as `/REPO/src/a.ts`, `/repo/SRC/new.ts` and `src/../SRC/a.ts`, with stat mapping them to `/repo/...`, all expected to be held.

The gate depends on `$.fs.stat({resolve:true}).realPath` to fold letter case. The plugin README states that "the letter case of existing folders resolve". Neither the REAL table nor ROWS has an entry where a differently-cased spelling of an existing folder resolves to the canonical path. The `fs.stat` mock looks paths up by exact key, so any differently-cased spelling stats as ENOENT. `placePath` then walks up to `/` and returns the path unchanged, and the gate allows it as outside the project. The case-folding fix is therefore unproven. Add case-folding entries to REAL, for example `'/REPO': '/repo'` and `'/repo/SRC': '/repo/src'`. Add ROWS that use them: `['/REPO/src/a.ts', false]`, `['/repo/SRC/new.ts', false]` and `['/REPO/.specclaw/changes/x/state.json', false]`. These rows must fail if `realPathOf` returns its input instead of `realPath`.

The diff changes plugin code under plugins/ (hooks, types and userConfig in plugin.json, tests, MOD.md), deletes the specclaw-mod plugin, and edits marketplace.json. No version is bumped in any plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json or marketplace.json plugins[] entry. The specclaw-mod entry carried 0.8.5, and the diff leaves the remaining plugins on whatever version they had. Bump every plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, every plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to the same new version.

The PR changes plugin code (new `show` and `fields` subcommands in specclaw-sync, a new plugin, and a specclaw test edit) but shows no version bump on any existing plugin. All plugins must share one version. If this is a release, every `plugin.json` (claude and codex) and every `marketplace.json` entry must move together; the new plugin is at 0.8.7 and specclaw-sync is not bumped in this diff.

The namespace enforces `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted`, but the Job pod sets no `seccompProfile` (RuntimeDefault) at pod or container level. The restricted profile requires one. The API server rejects the pods, and the Job sits with FailedCreate events. Add `seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}` to the pod securityContext.

The squid Deployment is applied into the `restricted` namespace with no securityContext: no runAsNonRoot, no allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, no capabilities drop and no seccompProfile. `ubuntu/squid` also normally starts as root. Admission rejects the pod, so there is no egress proxy and every fleet pod loses all connectivity. Set a non-root user, drop all capabilities, set seccomp RuntimeDefault, and make the paths squid writes to (logs, pid, cache) writable for that user.

`az keyvault secret show ... || az keyvault secret set ... --value __unset__` treats any `show` failure (throttle, network error, missing get permission, expired login) as 'secret does not exist'. It then overwrites a user's real registered credential with the placeholder. Only create the secret when the failure is specifically NotFound; otherwise die.

`fetch_credential` returns 1 both for 'no credential registered' (absent or `__unset__`) and for 'could not ask the vault' (az not logged in, network, 403). `check_gates` reports both as 'assignee has no registered credential' and marks the work item Failed with that reason. Distinguish a vault read error from not-found and surface it as an error, not as the assignee's problem.

The doc and header promise that `fields` 'always posts one comment' so the record survives. But the field PATCH runs first and `die`s on failure, so the comment is never posted. An invalid state transition or a bad field reference loses the whole record. Post the comment before the PATCH, or post it even when the PATCH fails.

Write-back uploads `auth.json` whenever its hash differs from the seed. It does not check that the file is valid JSON or non-empty. A truncated or corrupted file overwrites the assignee's working credential in the vault. Validate with `jq -e .` (and that it still has the expected token fields) before the PUT, and otherwise keep the old secret and report.

The 'one codex job per person' guarantee is a check-then-create (`codex_busy` then `launch_job`) with no atomic claim. README admits both can pass, yet the same README states the limit as a guarantee for safety reasons. The test (ac6) is single-session. Use an atomic claim, for example a per-assignee object created with `kubectl create` that fails if it already exists, and add a two-worker race test.

The 'finished → delete → create' replacement is a check-then-act. `kubectl delete job fleet-codex-<h>` deletes whatever Job currently has that name, not the finished Job that was read. Atomicity holds only for the create. The README and the fix claim the API itself enforces one codex job per person, and that is false on the replace path. Delete by UID, for example a `kubectl delete --raw` call with a uid precondition, or use a unique Job name per run plus a separate per-assignee claim object that is created atomically and released when the run ends. Add a race test where both workers start from a finished Job.

The loop was rewritten to `done < <(git diff -z ...)`, but a failure of that `git diff` is still invisible. The process substitution's exit status is ignored, so the loop sees zero files and the step exits 0. 'Could not list changed state files' reads as 'nothing approved'. Capture the diff output first, for example `mapfile -d '' -t files < <(...)` after a checked `git diff` into a variable or file, and fail the step if the diff fails.

The finished-Job race test is not deterministic. It starts two dispatches and relies on scheduling to interleave them between the `get job` read and the delete. The stub has no hook that forces worker B to read the old UID, worker A to delete and create, and worker B to then attempt its delete. If the UID precondition is removed or replaced by an unconditional delete, this test passes whenever B's delete lands before A's create or after B's own read. Add a deterministic test: seed a finished Job with an old UID, make the stub swap in a new claim with a new UID between the read and the `delete --raw`, then assert the delete is refused and the new claim survives. The stub already checks `preconditions.uid`, so only the interleaving hook is missing.

The test for the dispatch.yml fix only greps the pipeline source for the literal text `could not list changed state files"; exit 1`. It never runs the step with a failing `git diff`, and it checks no variants such as a shallow clone with no HEAD^1 or a git error. A textual match is not a test of behaviour. Extract the step's script, or run it with a stubbed `git` that exits non-zero, and assert a non-zero exit with the error logged.

The rewritten `status_at` runs `git cat-file -e "$1:$2" || echo absent`. That check fails for 'path not in that tree' and also for 'could not ask git' (bad or missing revision, missing or unfetchable object in a partial or blobless clone, repo error). Both cases print `absent` and return 0, so the failure the fix was meant to surface is turned back into a clean answer. Tell the cases apart. Take added/deleted/modified from `git diff -z --name-status` and only call `git show` for sides that must exist, or check `git rev-parse --verify` on the revision first. Treat any other failure as an error.

The behavioural tests now run the real step, but each fix has a single variant row. 'Failed diff' is only a root commit with no parent. 'Unreadable status' is only a truncated JSON in HEAD, and an unreadable HEAD^1 is not covered. Missing rows: valid-but-non-object JSON (`[]`, `"x"`), unreadable HEAD^1 content, a git error other than no-parent, and a state.json deleted in HEAD. The 'no dispatch when nothing flipped' case uses an empty commit, so the diff list is empty and the `before != approved` comparison is never reached. A changed state.json that stays approved→approved is untested, so removing the `before` check would keep every test green. Make the tests table-driven over the variants, including a draft→approved flip, an approved→approved edit, and an added file.

This round adds a fail-closed branch: when `kubectl get job` fails with anything other than NotFound, the code dies. The stub gained a NotFound message, but no test makes `get job` fail with a different error (Forbidden, timeout, connection refused) and asserts the dispatch is refused and nothing is created. Replacing `die` with `return 0` would leave all tests green. Add rows for the non-NotFound errors and assert that no Job or claim is created.

The write-back container mounts the same `home` emptyDir that the agent wrote to, and runs with HOME=/home/agent. `writeback.sh` then calls `curl` and `jq` without disabling their per-user config. `curl` reads `~/.curlrc` and `jq` reads `~/.jq`. Agent code, including code steered by prompt injection, can therefore plant a `.curlrc` that changes the requests made while AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET is in the environment. This breaks the README's claim that the vault writer credential is out of the agent's reach. The README also says this service principal may set every `codex-auth-*` secret, which in Key Vault RBAC means vault scope, so it can overwrite other users' credentials. Fix: mount only `.codex/auth.json`, read-only, into write-back, and set HOME to a fresh emptyDir there. Also call `curl -q` (it must be the first argument) and `jq` with `-L /dev/null`, or set HOME to an empty directory for each call.

Consent is accepted from any `fleet:auto` tag on the work item, but the README says the tag is 'set by the assignee' and that assignment 'must not spend their plan without their say'. The code never checks who added the tag. Fix: read the work item updates or revisions and accept the tag only when the revision that added it has System.ChangedBy equal to the assignee. Add a test where someone else added the tag.

Tags are compared to `fleet:auto` case-sensitively. Azure DevOps tags are case-insensitive, and a new tag takes the casing of an existing tag in the project. Compare with `lower`, and add `Fleet:Auto` and `FLEET:AUTO` rows to the AC4d table.

`cfg_val` swallows every python3 failure with `2>/dev/null || true` and returns the default. So 'could not read config.yaml' (python3 missing, file missing, parse error) reads the same as 'key not set'. The README's pipeline prerequisites do not list python3. Fail when the config read itself fails, and use the default only when the key is truly absent.

`delete_job_if_uid` ends in `|| true`. A delete that fails for any reason (Forbidden, connection refused, timeout) is hidden, and the later AlreadyExists is reported as 'assignee already has an unfinished codex job'. The work item is then marked Failed with that false reason. Only a precondition (UID) conflict should map to 'busy'. Any other delete error should die with the real error. Add a test row for each.

Only `HEAD^1..HEAD` is compared, with `fetchDepth: 2`. One CI run can cover a push of several commits (a direct push, or a rebase/fast-forward merge). An approval in any commit other than the last one is never seen. Diff against the commit of the last successful run, or against the push's before-SHA, with enough fetch depth.

The Job clones `--branch $FLEET_REF` (default `main`) at pod start, not the commit whose approval triggered the dispatch. The commit actually built is never recorded on the work item. Pass Build.SourceVersion through dispatch, check out that exact SHA, and record it in the run fields.

The agent container sets `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, but there is no writable /tmp and no TMPDIR. claude and codex write temporary files to os.tmpdir(), for example Claude Code's Bash-tool cwd files under /tmp, and so do git and python tempfile. The hardening covered the root filesystem but not every writable path the agents need. Mount an emptyDir at /tmp, or set TMPDIR to a path under /fleet/work.

After a failed clone, the fallback tracker directory has a status.md but no config.yaml. `specclaw-azdo-issue fields` therefore finds no `azdo.fleet_states` mapping and posts only a comment, and System.State stays at Dispatched. The README says a clone failure 'still marks the work item Failed'. Copy or pass the state and field mapping into the pod, for example as env or a ConfigMap, and write it into the fallback config.yaml. Add a test that checks a state PATCH is made on clone failure.

The diff changes plugin code (new `updates` subcommand in specclaw-sync, new specclaw-fleet files) but no `plugin.json` (claude or codex) or `marketplace.json` version is bumped. All plugins must share one version and the version must change when plugin code changes. This was already reported last round and is still unfixed.

Dispatch records `commit=$F_COMMIT` (launch.sh) and the pod then records `commit=<HEAD of clone>` under the same key. The `fields` command writes one mapped field per key, so the second write replaces the first. The README says 'The work item records both commits', but only the built tip survives. Use distinct keys (for example `commit` and `dispatched_commit`), map both, and test that both reach the fields call.

The previous finding listed 'file missing' as a read failure that must fail. The fix makes a missing config.yaml `sys.exit(0)`, so it still returns the default, exactly like 'key not set'. This is an instance fix of the python3 case only. A missing config must fail (the tracker fallback writes its own config.yaml, so a hard failure is safe). Also, callers that substitute `$(cfg_val ...)` inside a larger string, for example `"branch=$(cfg_val git.branch_prefix specclaw/)$F_CHANGE"` in launch.sh, lose the new `die`, because it only exits the subshell.

The fix to make `cfg_val` fail closed ships no test at all. No test file in the diff exercises an unreadable config, a missing python3, or a missing file. Add a table of variants (python3 absent from PATH, config.yaml unreadable, config.yaml absent, key absent -> default) that fails without the fix.

`cfg_block` is a second config parser (awk, exact match `$0 == "azdo:"`) beside the python parser in `cfg_val`. They can disagree. A section header with a trailing comment or whitespace (the shipped template annotates keys with trailing comments) is found by a regex section parser but not by the exact-match awk. Use one parser, or make both share the header rule.

`base_commit` silently falls back to `HEAD^1` when `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` is empty. That reintroduces the multi-commit hole the change fixes, with no error or log line. A missing token should fail the step, not widen or narrow the comparison silently. Only a successful lookup that returns no previous run should fall back to the parent commit.

The consent fix adds a fail-closed branch (`die` when the history cannot be read) and history-based rules, but the tests cover only 'added by mallory' and 'added by unknown'. Missing variants: the `updates` read failing; the tag removed and re-added by someone else after the assignee added it; the tag present with no add event in the history. Also, a history read failure kills dispatch even when the requester is the assignee, which is valid consent through the second path. Check the requester first, or test that this is intended.

The previous finding asked for a test that a state PATCH is made on clone failure. `specclaw-azdo-issue` is stubbed with `exit 0`, so the test only checks that a hand-written string landed in the fallback config.yaml. It never shows the real `fields` parser turning that file into a state change.

When `--writer` and `fleet.vault_writer` are both unset, onboarding silently skips the writer grant and prints 'Onboarded'. `fleet.vault_writer` is not in the README's config example. The write-back then fails with a 403 and the failure message blames the assignee ('re-run login'), when the cause is a missing admin grant. Require the writer, or warn loudly that codex refresh will not persist.

Plugin code under plugins/ changes (specclaw-fleet lib, image and pipeline files, and earlier in the PR the specclaw-sync `updates` subcommand), but no plugin version is bumped. This was reported last round and is still unfixed. Bump `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and every `plugins[]` entry in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to one identical new version.

The fail-closed `cfg_val` is an instance fix. Its `die` and `exit 1` only end the command-substitution subshell, so any caller that does not add `|| die` keeps going with an empty value. `writer="${writer:-$(cfg_val fleet.vault_writer "")}"` is such a caller. `prefix="$(cfg_val git.branch_prefix specclaw/)"` in launch.sh:66 has the same gap and depends on `set -e` being active. Make every caller check the result (`v="$(cfg_val ...)" || exit 1`), or have `cfg_val` signal failure in a way the shell cannot swallow. Also give the new warning different text when the config could not be read.

`rc` is read from `$STATUS/exit`. The agent initContainer writes that file on a read-write `status` volume, so agent code (including prompt-injected code) controls it. `rc` is then evaluated in bash arithmetic: `$(( rc != 0 ? rc : 3 ))` in `fail()` and on the last line. Bash arithmetic recursively evaluates a variable's value, and an array subscript inside that value runs command substitution. So agent-controlled text executes inside the write-back container, which holds `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` for the writer service principal. Validate before any use: `[[ "$rc" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] || rc=1`, placed right after the read. Add a variant test that writes non-numeric payloads to `status/exit` (`a[$(touch x)]`, `1+1`, empty) and asserts nothing runs and the exit code is sane.

The base is 'last *succeeded* run', but the step fails (`failed=1`) whenever any single dispatch is refused. A refusal is often permanent (no consent, no credential, busy codex). After one, every later run diffs from the same stale green commit and re-dispatches the changes that were already dispatched. Two overlapping runs also share the same base and both dispatch the same approval. The range must be 'since the last processed commit', not 'since the last green run'. Record processed commits, or let refusals not fail the run, and dedupe by change plus dispatched commit (e.g. check for an existing Job or work-item record for that commit).

`auto_tagged_by` reads a single page of `workitems/{id}/updates`: `cmd_updates` passes no `$top`/`$skip` and does not follow continuation. A partial history is treated as complete, and the 'last add event' is taken from that page. Page through all updates (or read revisions until fewer than `$top` come back), and fail closed if paging cannot complete. Add a variant test with a multi-page history.

Approval is read at the dispatched commit, but the pod builds the tip of FLEET_REF. It checks only that the dispatched commit is an ancestor of the tip, never that the proposal is still approved there. The README states 'the base is fresh and still contains the approval', which the code does not guarantee. Re-read `.phases.proposal.status` from the cloned HEAD's state.json and record `failed`/`not-approved-at-ref` before running the agent.

The value reader matches only keys at exactly two spaces of indentation (`^  key:`), and it splits on the first `#` even inside quotes. A key that is present in valid YAML but indented differently, or that holds a quoted `#`, reads as absent and falls back to the default silently. The fallback for `deadline_minutes` is a wider limit. Derive the child indent from the first non-blank line under the section, honour quotes when stripping comments, and fail when a key exists but cannot be parsed.

Moving settings from the committed config.yaml to pipeline parameters lets anyone who can queue a run override them. `image`, `namespace`, `defaultAgent` and `deadlineMinutes` have no `values:` allowlist in dispatch.yml. Only agent and deadline are validated in `parse_dispatch_args`. `F_IMAGE` and `F_NS` go unvalidated into `kubectl -n` and the rendered Job manifest, so a multi-line value can also inject extra pod-spec fields. Give the parameters a `values:` allowlist or restrict who can queue, and validate `F_IMAGE`, `F_NS` and `F_REF` against a strict charset regex (single line, no whitespace or quotes).

Requester-is-assignee consent was safe when a run only dispatched the approval in its own commit range. The pipeline now scans every approved-not-started change on each run, so the requester shortcut covers every pending change assigned to that person, not just the one they pushed. Tie requester consent to the change that triggered the run (for example, only when the requester authored the approving commit), or require fleet:auto for changes the run did not itself approve.

`F_AZDO_CONFIG="$(cat config.yaml 2>/dev/null || true)"` turns a missing or unreadable config.yaml into an empty mapping, and dispatch carries on. The old code failed closed here, and the tests for that were deleted. AC11 now asserts that dispatch works with no config.yaml. The whole file is also copied into the Job env, where it is readable via `kubectl get job`; the old code passed only the azdo block. Fail when the file cannot be read, and pass only the azdo block.

The idempotency record (the fleet:dispatched tag) is written after the Job exists and is only warned about if it fails. The `already_handled` read-then-act is not an atomic claim. `batch: true` serialises only pipeline runs, not a manual `specclaw-fleet dispatch` running alongside one. There is no race test. Claim before creating the Job (a deterministic Job name so a second create gets AlreadyExists, or tag first and abort on failure), and also check for an existing Job for the change.

The page merge passes the accumulated history and each page as python argv (`"$all" "$page"`), and its exit status is not checked. A single argument over about 128 KB fails with E2BIG on Linux, and the failure leaves `all` empty with no message. A real 200-update page (revisedBy identity objects) is well above that. Merge via stdin or a temp file and add `|| die` to every step. The new tests use `{"id":i}` stubs, so they never exercise realistic page sizes or the exactly-200 boundary.

The not-approved-at-ref recheck (entrypoint.sh:67) is a fail-closed branch with one test row: status=draft. The `2>/dev/null` and `// empty` paths are untested. Add rows for state.json missing at the ref, truncated or non-object JSON, `.phases.proposal` absent, and status `none`/`approved ` variants. Each should record not-approved-at-ref and never reach `run_agent`.

This diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet and plugins/specclaw-sync (new `tag` subcommand, paged `updates`, dispatch behaviour) but touches no `plugin.json` or `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` version. All claude and codex plugin.json files and every marketplace.json entry must carry the same bumped version. If an earlier commit on this branch already bumped all of them, ignore this.

In `cmd_claim`, any failure of the claim PATCH (`ado_patch_json ... || { ...; exit 3; }`) is reported as 'changed while claiming' with exit 3. `claim_change` turns exit 3 into 'already handled or claimed by another dispatch', and the pipeline treats 3 as a clean skip. An auth error, 5xx, timeout or network failure therefore reads as 'someone else won the race'. Only a real rev conflict (HTTP 409/412) should exit 3. Every other PATCH failure should `die` (exit 1) so the pipeline step fails. The new test only stubs the PATCH failure as curl exit 22 and expects 3, so it cannot tell the two cases apart; add a variant for a non-conflict failure.

The busy codex slot now exits 5, which the pipeline swallows silently (`0|3|5) ;;`), leaves the change untagged, and no longer marks the work item Failed or warns. README says 'a later run retries it', but the pipeline only triggers when a `state.json` changes on main, so nothing guarantees a later run happens. Before this round the same condition produced a visible refusal and a pipeline warning. Emit a `##vso[task.logissue type=warning]` for exit 5 and fix the README claim, or add a scheduled trigger.

The new claim-release branch in `launch_job` (untag after `create_manifests` fails) is tested only for the busy case (AC4f). There is no row for the other failures that happen after the claim: `kubectl create` of the Secret or Job failing with Forbidden, a timeout or a connection error, or the untag itself failing (the `warn` path). If the release is dropped, or only handles exit 5, no test fails. Add table rows for those variants asserting the claim directory is gone and the exit code is propagated.

This diff changes code under plugins/specclaw-fleet and plugins/specclaw-sync (new `claim` and `untag` subcommands, exit code 5, validation) but touches no plugin.json or marketplace.json version. The previous round raised this and it is still unaddressed in the diff. All claude and codex plugin.json files and every marketplace.json entry must carry one identical bumped version. Ignore this only if an earlier commit on the branch already bumped all of them.

The kubectl stub's create branch is `[[ -n CREATE_ERR ]] && grep -q "^kind: ${CREATE_KIND:-Job}" && {...}`. The `grep -q` reads all of stdin. When CREATE_KIND=Secret, the first `create -f -` is the Job, which does not match, so the grep drains the pipe and `doc="$(cat)"` is empty. The Job is then recorded under an empty name, the later `get job` finds no uid, and `create_manifests` takes the `[[ -z "$uid" ]]` branch. The `render_secret | kubectl create` failure path is never reached, so the new 'Secret create fails' rows exercise the empty-uid case instead. The stub should buffer stdin first (`doc="$(cat)"`) and then match on `$doc`. Add a row where the Job is created and uid is read, and only the Secret create fails.

After a failed PATCH, `tag_update` treats any change in rev as someone else's concurrent edit and retries. A PATCH that was applied server-side but whose response was lost (timeout, reset) also bumps rev. The retry then re-reads the item and finds our own tag. In strict (claim) mode that returns exit 3, 'already holds the tag'. `claim_change` and the pipeline read exit 3 as 'claimed by another dispatch' and skip silently. The work item is left tagged fleet:dispatched with no Job and no failure signal, and later runs skip it as already handled. 'Could not tell whether our write landed' should not read as 'someone else won'. Fix: remember that an earlier attempt of ours failed with an unknown outcome, and if the next read shows the tag held with rev == old+1, treat it as ours (success). Or fail with exit 1 so the step reports an error instead of a clean skip.

Two different cases share one path. A work item that never opted in (no `fleet:auto` tag at all) is handled like a bad consent (tag added by someone else). Both call `refuse`, which sets the item to the mapped `Failed` state and tags it `fleet:refused`. The pipeline scans every approved change with `phase: proposal` on each run, so every approved change meant for a human gets moved to Failed in Boards. This contradicts the README, which says dispatch 'runs only when the work item carries the tag fleet:auto'. Fix: when `has_auto_tag` is false, skip without writing anything (for example, exit 3 or a new 'not opted in' code that the pipeline ignores). Keep `refuse` for a tag added by someone else, and for credential and vault failures.

AZDO_ORG is taken as `basename` of SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI. That only works for `https://dev.azure.com/<org>/`. For the legacy `https://<org>.visualstudio.com/` form, which the README's egress list explicitly allows, the result is the whole host name. Every specclaw-azdo-issue call then goes to `dev.azure.com/<org>.visualstudio.com/...` and fails. Fix: parse both URL forms, or pass the org explicitly as a pipeline variable.

FLEET_REF is set from `$(Build.SourceBranchName)`. That variable holds only the last path segment of the branch, so it handles only single-segment branch names. A manual queue on any branch with a slash passes the wrong ref, while FLEET_COMMIT is that branch's HEAD. Fix: use `Build.SourceBranch` with the `refs/heads/` prefix removed.

`attempt` counts the Jobs that currently carry the change label. That count is not the attempt number. The codex Job has a fixed name and `claim_codex_slot` deletes the previous finished one first. Claude Jobs are garbage-collected after `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400`. Also, `label_value` collapses distinct change names (`049 x` and `049-x`) onto one label. So the recorded FleetAttempt resets or merges. Fix: derive the attempt from the work item's history or from a stored counter, not from live Jobs.

The image that runs the agent decides the outcome, through the claude/codex versions and the specclaw plugin code baked into it. It defaults to the mutable tag `specclaw-fleet:latest`. The run record on the work item stores job, agent, cluster and commits, but not the image reference or its digest. Fix: record `image=$F_IMAGE`, and preferably the resolved digest, in `record_run`. Also require a digest or an explicit tag instead of defaulting to `:latest`.

The diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (new commands, a new image layout, new pipelines, new skills). It bumps none of the shared versions: plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Bump all of them together to one new version.

The gates run against the operator's local working tree, but the default path only queues the pipeline. `az pipelines run` is given no change name, so the pipeline scans and dispatches every approved change on `FLEET_REF`, and does nothing for this one if its state.json on that branch is not approved or not at phase 'proposal'. Trigger still prints `{ok:true, mode:pipeline, run:...}`, so 'queued' reads as 'will be dispatched'. Pass the change to the pipeline as a parameter, or verify that the pushed ref carries the approval before reporting success.

`trigger_gates` repeats the dispatch gate sequence (assignee, fleet:auto consent, credential lookup) and takes the agent from the operator's local `FLEET_DEFAULT_AGENT`. The pipeline dispatches with its own `fleetDefaultAgent` variable. The two copies can pick different agents. Trigger also skips the codex-busy check. Pass an explicit agent to the pipeline, or reuse `check_gates`.

The hosted agent clones specclaw from github.com/chan4lk/specclaw at `fleetSpecclawRef`, a mutable tag name. That code then runs with the kube service connection and the ARM service principal. The commit actually executed is never recorded. Resolve the ref to a full commit SHA, pin to the SHA, and log it.

The no-overwrite guard treats any failure of `docker manifest inspect` as 'tag does not exist'. Auth errors, rate limits, network failures and registry 5xx all take the same path as a genuine 404. Only a confirmed 'manifest unknown' response should let the push proceed. Any other failure should fail the job. Capture stderr and match the not-found message, or use `docker buildx imagetools inspect` and branch on the error text.

A check that returns 2 (skipped, so not actually run) is counted as skipped and does not fail the run. `failed == 0` then prints 'doctor: all checks ok (N skipped)' and exits 0. A check that could not run reads as a pass. Treat skipped checks as unknown. Print something like 'doctor: incomplete, N checks did not run' and return non-zero, or at least never use the 'all checks ok' wording when skipped > 0.

The previous finding offered two fixes: pass an explicit agent, or reuse `check_gates`. Only the agent was fixed. `trigger_gates` is still a second copy of the dispatch gate sequence (assignee, consent, credential), and it still skips the codex-busy check. The two copies can disagree on any gate, and trigger reports success for a run the pipeline will skip. Reuse `check_gates` from dispatch, or add the busy check here, and have the queued path report refusals instead of `ok:true`.

This is an instance fix. Only the assignee and consent steps now share `gate_owner`. `trigger_gates` still re-implements the rest of the dispatch gate sequence: the credential lookup and its case mapping. It still skips the `codex_busy` check and `already_handled`. It also skips the proposal-approved check and the work-item-id check that `check_gates` makes. The previous round asked to reuse `check_gates` or add the busy check, and the queued path should report refusals instead of `ok:true`. Neither was done. Reuse `check_gates` (parameterised so it does not exit or launch), or move the whole gate sequence, including the busy and already-handled checks, into one shared function that both callers use.

The confirmed-404 match is wrong in both directions. `docker manifest inspect` reports a missing tag as `no such manifest: ...`, which the pattern does not match. The pattern `not found` is also too broad: it matches `docker: command not found` and similar unrelated errors. The guard can therefore fail a genuine first publish, or treat a non-404 failure as proof that the tag is absent. Use `docker buildx imagetools inspect` or the registry HTTP status and match only the exact not-found signals (`manifest unknown`, `no such manifest`, HTTP 404). Treat everything else as a failure.

The fixes for the three previous majors have no variant tests. The doctor test covers only one case: skipped > 0 with failed == 0. It does not cover failed > 0 with skipped > 0 (exit 1 and its wording), or several skipped checks. There is no test that `trigger_gates` and `check_gates` agree across the gate outcomes (no tag, no assignee, tagger is not the assignee, history unreadable, busy). The workflow guard has no test for the 404, auth-error and network-error variants. `gate_owner` return codes 10/11/12/13 are never exercised through both callers.

The reorder in `fleet_trigger` moved the approval gate behind two mutating steps. The `--retry` untag calls and `trigger_work_item` (which creates a work item under `--create`) now run before `check_gates` calls `trigger_ref_approved`. Before this round, `trigger_ref_approved` ran first. The SKILL.md claim that trigger 'writes nothing' while checking is false for these two paths. Fix: run `parse_dispatch_args`, `check_gates` and the busy check first. The work-item creation and the untag calls would run only after the gates pass (create when no work item exists; untag only if `--retry` is given). Note that `check_gates` already refuses when there is no work item, so the order needs care for `--create`: run the approval check before creating, then re-run the full gates.

`trigger_codex_busy` uses `F_NS`, but `parse_dispatch_args` now skips `parse_pod_inputs` in check-only mode, and that function is what sets the pod/namespace inputs. If `F_NS` is not set elsewhere, kubectl runs with `-n ''` or under `set -u` errors. `-n ''` queries the context's default namespace, so it looks in the wrong place and gets NotFound. A NotFound result returns 0, and the JSON then reports `codex_busy_check: "done"`. This is a check that did not really run, reported as clear. Fix: resolve the namespace and hash explicitly for check-only mode, and test that the busy check reads the same namespace dispatch uses.

The busy check is still a second copy of dispatch's logic. `trigger_codex_busy` re-implements the codex-slot check with its own kubectl call, its own NotFound handling and its own 'unknown means pass' fallback, instead of sharing one function with dispatch. The previous round asked for one shared gate sequence, and the claim that trigger 'runs exactly dispatch's gates' does not hold for this gate. Move the busy check into one function called from `check_gates` (with the check-only variant deciding what to do on an unreadable cluster), and delete the trigger copy.

The parity table covers only gate_owner outcomes and 'handled'. The previous round asked for parity across all gate outcomes, including busy. Missing rows: busy codex slot, the credential-missing and Key Vault-unreadable outcomes, an unapproved proposal and a missing work item. The busy-check copy is the one most likely to drift, and no test would notice.

The codex Job name is now spelled two ways. `codex_slot_state` reads the hard-coded `fleet-codex-$F_HASH`, while `delete_job_if_uid` and `create_job` still use `$F_JOB`. The old `claim_codex_slot` read `$F_JOB`, so this is a regression. The literal was most likely added because check-only mode skips `parse_pod_inputs`, so `F_JOB` is unset there. Derive the name once (for example a `codex_job_name` function used by the reader, the deleter and `render_job`), or resolve `F_JOB` in check-only mode too.

The reorder fix (gates before any write) has no variant test. The write detector greps only `azdo-issue (fields|tag|claim)` and `pipelines run`, so `azdo-issue untag` and work-item creation are not detected. No row runs `trigger --retry` or `trigger --create`. Add rows that run those flags against a refused or unapproved change and assert that no untag or create call reached the stubs.

The unparsable-JSON fix covers only the case where jq exits non-zero. If kubectl exits 0 with empty stdout, jq prints nothing and exits 0, so `codex_slot_state` returns an empty string. `claim_codex_slot` has no case for an empty state, so it proceeds as if the slot were free. The same goes for any caller that treats an unknown state as free. Reject empty or unknown output explicitly, for example `s=$(jq ...) || s=''; [[ -n $s ]] || s='error unparsable Job JSON'`, or add a `*) die` default branch. A `finished null` result (no `.metadata.uid`) should also be an error. The fix also ships with no test that feeds the stub unparsable, empty or non-object Job JSON.

The new write-before-gate rows assert only the exit code and message through `gate`. They do not assert that no `azdo-issue untag`, `azdo-issue create`, `fields`, `tag`, `claim` or `pipelines run` call reached `$CALLS`. Reverting the reorder would still return the same rc and message while writing first, so the rows do not fail without the fix. Every row also passes `--retry` or `--create` against a change that is merely unapproved or lacks consent. There is no row for a change carrying the `fleet:refused` tag, which is where untag matters. There is no `--create` row where the work item is missing and a later gate fails, such as a missing credential. Add those rows and assert that `$CALLS` holds no write command. The ac18 detector now matches `untag|create`, but its `row()` runs `trigger` without `--retry` or `--create`, so that widening exercises nothing.

This is an instance fix of the previous B2 finding. The one new row (fleet:refused + --retry + missing claude credential) is checked through `gate`, which asserts only rc and message. It still never asserts that `$CALLS` holds no `azdo-issue untag`, `create`, `fields`, `tag`, `claim` or `pipelines run`. The requested `--create` row, where the work item is missing and a later gate fails, was not added. The ac18 detector widening still exercises nothing, because its `row()` does not pass `--retry` or `--create`. Assert that `$CALLS` has no write command in these rows and add the `--create` + missing-credential row.

The junk-Job-JSON test only asserts the dispatch path. The `trigger` call on each row discards its result with `|| true`, so the check-only path (`check_only_busy`, T_BUSY_CHECK) is never verified against empty, unparsable, non-object or uid-less JSON. AC8 covers only GET_ERR, not junk output. Assert that `codex_busy_check` starts with `not-run` for every junk row.

This commit changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet and bumps no version. The earlier finding asked for a bump and this round did not make one. Bump every plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, every plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to one new identical version.

trigger reads approval from the pushed ref (FETCH_HEAD), but it reads every other gate input from the local working tree. The work-item line in status.md comes from local files, and with --direct the approval is re-read by dispatch's local proposal_approved and the dispatched commit comes from local HEAD. The queued pipeline and the pod read the pushed tree, so trigger's verdict can disagree with the real one. Fix: read status.md (work item id) from FETCH_HEAD too. On --direct, keep the pushed-ref reader (stay check-only for approval) and set F_COMMIT to the FETCH_HEAD commit instead of local HEAD.

FLEET_REF is set from $(Build.SourceBranchName), which is only the last path segment of the branch. trigger queues the pipeline with `--branch ${FLEET_REF:-main}`, and dispatch accepts refs containing '/'. Any slashed branch is therefore cloned under the wrong name. The same defect is in pipelines/dispatch.yml:81. Fix: use $(Build.SourceBranch) with the refs/heads/ prefix stripped.

The run record persisted on the work item names the job, cluster, commit and requester. It does not record which image (FLEET_IMAGE) or which Claude release (F_CLAUDE_VERSION) executed the run. Both decide the outcome, and the self-hosted template's default image is the mutable `specclaw-fleet:latest` (pipelines/dispatch.yml:14). Fix: add image=$F_IMAGE and claude_version=$F_CLAUDE_VERSION to record_run (or to the pod's state=running record). Pin the default image to a tag or digest.

The commit changes code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (lib/, pipelines/, k8s/, skills/) but the diff bumps no version. No plugin.json (.claude-plugin or .codex-plugin) and no entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json is touched. The new default image tag 0.8.9 is also tied to a plugin version that does not change here. Bump every plugin.json and every marketplace.json plugins[] entry to the same new version.

The FLEET_REF fix (a B1 major) ships a single variant row: refs/heads/feature/fleet-x. Missing rows are refs/heads/main, an already-bare 'main', unset or empty, and a non-branch ref such as refs/tags/x or refs/pull/1/merge. The test extracts the step only from pipelines/dispatch.yml (tests/lib/pipeline-env.sh), so the identical edit in pipelines/dispatch-hosted.yml has no test. The two copies can drift. Make the test table-driven over these variants and run it against both templates.

F_COMMIT and F_REPO now come from FLEET_DISPATCH_COMMIT and FLEET_REPO_URL, taken from the environment with no validation. The other inputs are validated (FLEET_IMAGE, FLEET_NAMESPACE, F_REF). Plain `specclaw-fleet dispatch` honours these variables too, so the approval gate can be checked against the local tree while a different commit or repo is dispatched. Only trigger should set these. Validate the commit as ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ and the URL as an expected https form, or pass them as explicit internal arguments instead of ambient env vars.

The default image reference ghcr.io/chan4lk/specclaw-fleet:0.8.9 is hard-coded in lib/dispatch.sh, in pipelines/dispatch.yml (fleetImage), and in the ac5 test. These copies must be bumped together on every release. If dispatch-hosted.yml carries its own default, it is a fourth copy that this commit did not touch. Keep one source (for example, derive the tag from the plugin version) and have the other places read it.

There are two copies of the 'pending' rule, and they disagree. trigger (and dispatch's `proposal_approved`) only checks `.phases.proposal.status == "approved"`. The pipeline step it queues (dispatch.yml:60, dispatch-hosted.yml) also requires `.phase == "proposal"` and silently skips everything else. trigger therefore reports gates passed and queues a run that does nothing, and nothing is recorded on the work item, although its JSON note says the outcome lands there. Fix: put the pending predicate in one place and use it in both. Either trigger applies the phase check and refuses with a clear message, or the pipeline dispatches the named change without the phase filter when `change` is set.

The cluster is selected in two different ways.
- `doctor` targets `FLEET_KUBE_CONTEXT` (doctor-checks.sh:3), and the setup skill tells the operator to set it and never switch their current context.
- `dispatch`/`trigger` call bare `kubectl` everywhere: create_job, the Secret, the codex slot read and delete, and `current-context` for the run record.

Fix: route every dispatch/trigger kubectl call through one helper that applies `--context "$FLEET_KUBE_CONTEXT"` when it is set, the way `dk` does.

`prepare_workspace` treats a failed `git ls-remote` the same as 'no existing change branch': the empty `ref` returns 0. A failed fetch/checkout returns non-zero, but `run_agent` ignores it. Either way the agent starts fresh from the base ref. Fix: check the `ls-remote` exit status separately from an empty result, and make `run_agent` stop (record a `resume-failed` exit) when lookup, fetch or checkout fails.

The seed home installs only the `specclaw` and `specclaw-sync` Claude plugins. The pod prompt (entrypoint.sh PROMPT) still tells the agent to 'run the specclaw-review loop as its skill describes', and that skill lives in `specclaw-review`, which is not installed. Only its bin is on PATH. The headless agent is told to use a skill it does not have, and nothing stops or flags this. Fix: also `claude plugin install specclaw-review@chan4lk` (and specclaw-extras if the lifecycle needs it), and add an image test that the seeded plugin list covers every skill the prompt names.

Only the normal exit path saves the agent's work. After `run_agent` it calls `push_change_branch` and `ensure_pr`. The deadline path does not: `on_term` (the in-pod watchdog, or a kubelet SIGTERM) kills the agent, records `failed/deadline` and calls `finish` with no push and no draft PR. The commits live only in the `work` emptyDir, so they are lost when the Pod goes. This contradicts the run skill ('Work always lands on the change branch, and a retry resumes it'; 'Every finished run that pushed work gets a PR'). Fix: in `on_term`, after killing the agent and only once the clone and workspace exist, run the same `push_change_branch` / `ensure_pr` / `record` sequence that the normal path uses, then call `finish 143`. Add rows to the deadline test for the claude and codex agents, and for a TERM that arrives before the agent starts.

Several doctor checks report 'missing' or 'wrong' when they could not ask at all. This includes no network, ghcr/az/kubectl being unreachable, and az not logged in:
